events.title: First Parliament of Great Britain Meets
events.description: Following the Acts of Union, the first Parliament of Great Britain convened. It united the former English and Scottish parliaments into a single legislature at Westminster.
events.significance: It marked the start of the parliamentary union that shaped the modern British state.

events.title: Hungarian Revolution Begins
events.description: Protests in Budapest grew into a nationwide uprising against Soviet-backed rule. Hungarians demanded political freedom and an end to Soviet domination.
events.significance: Soviet forces crushed the revolt, but it became a lasting symbol of resistance in the Cold War. Hungary now commemorates October 23 as a national day.

events.title: Birth of Pelé
events.description: Edson Arantes do Nascimento was born in Brazil. He became one of the greatest footballers of all time.
events.significance: Pelé won three World Cups with Brazil and helped turn football into a truly global sport.

events.title: Beirut Barracks Bombings
events.description: Two truck bombs struck American and French military barracks in Beirut during the Lebanese Civil War. About 300 service members were killed.
events.significance: It was among the deadliest attacks on U.S. forces in decades. It also led to the withdrawal of international peacekeepers from Lebanon.

events.title: Moscow Dubrovka Theater Hostage Crisis
events.description: About 50 Chechen militants led by Movsar Barayev seized a Moscow theater during a performance of the musical Nord-Ost. They took hundreds of audience members and performers hostage.
events.significance: The siege ended after three days. It became one of the most notorious hostage crises in modern Russian history and shaped the country's security policies.
